questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The courses available and being able to understand and speak the language of the destination.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Unfortunately, there were long periods of strike from the teachers during my semester abroad. This had a big–and negative–impact on one's involvement in the courses and the feeling of becoming absorbed in them; both facets were lacking, essentially, due to teachers' absence and too big of an amount of independence.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was convenient and easy, University of Edinburgh took good care of me as a visiting student. I got a 'personal tutor' with whom an introductory meeting was mandatory, and this gave one a great landing in a new university and system.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Introductory mails from a 'Visiting Students Office' as well as being added to Facebook groups etc. Also, I had the meeting with my personal tutor as described above.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy – some friends and I were lucky to find a suitable Airbnb after having been recommended to look for Airbnb's rather than student accommodation.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Find a nice area.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was a long process but it was solvable.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Emails with the 'Visiting Students Office' and my personal tutor.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: My personal tutor helped me a great deal, it was definitely much easier and more convenient to be in contact with her rather than the office. Mails were answered faster and she could guide me more on a personal level. The office seemed very stressed with getting all students' courses sorted and therefore I felt a lack of surplus from the administration.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Remember to read carefully whether the course is available to you or not, and if you have a personal tutor, be sure to use them instead of the administration's office.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The courses and teachers were good but again, my experience of the academic programme was highly influenced by the strikes.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was roughly what I expected, although I was surprised by the vert small amount of hours in class – it was generally more independent than I thought.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I had very few lectures at my host institution and instead seminars and 'workshops'. This is almost the complete opposite of UCPH at which place I have lectures only, mostly. I missed having lectures and UoE–the academic engagement became too independently based–yet I also enjoyed the bigger amount of class discussion and so-called 'seminars'.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: The Arts in the Age of the Great Caliphs 650-1250 (HIAR10165), Sustainable Sculpture Practice (ARTX08064), Critical and Cultural Theories of Contemporary Art (ARTX08087)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I highly recommend The Arts in the Age of the Great Caliphs 650-1250 (HIAR10165) since it explores Islamic visual culture during a certain period in time and therefore takes another art historical perspective than the euro-centric one which is highly dominant in UCPH and other universities.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Beer.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: General grocery shopping was less expensive than expected, though the amount of pints bought and the cost of them, exceeded my expectation.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of societies were available, something for everyone.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Pole dancing.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Save up money for trips to the highlands, it is more expensive than I thought.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Edinburgh is a VERY international city, not to mention the university itself, so don't expect meeting a lot of Scots. Be open to students but be even more open to people in coffee bars, bars, etc., you are likely to meet local friends here if you're open and curious.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The were much more violence amongst people in the nightlife and even in the everyday, this was something to get used to yet I never felt in danger.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The pub culture, music scene, and the lovely dialect.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Find someone to study with (if you have the same small amount of actual classes as I had), be open to people outside of the university, and expect to spend a lot of money on pints.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You don't spend a lot of time at the university so find a nice area to base yourself in and use that area. Study at the coffee places, find the chill bars, listen to live music in pubs.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The experience of studying in a different culture and learning some Scottish slang.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Coming to terms with how young people were at the host institution. It felt more like Danish gymnasium than uni.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: You will understand the Scots eventually, give it time.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
